attempts.label: DANDI:001828
attempts.paper_title: Anxa1+ dopamine neuron vulnerability defines prodromal Parkinson’s disease bradykinesia and procedural motor learning impairment
attempts.entry_title: Anxa1+ dopamine neurons, behaviour and photometry (Mantas, Contestabile, Skara et al. 2024)
attempts.summary: Of the paper's main findings, the slower locomotion of Anxa1-silenced mice held in this data, and so did the negative correlation of cCP dopamine with speed. The ramp of Anxa1 and DAT axon signals to the water-drop touch did not reproduce, and neither did the positive correlation of Anxa1 axon activity with speed (p = 0.064 to 0.21). The loss of Anxa1 neurons in early Parkinson models, the anatomy and the motif analyses could not be tested, because the dandiset holds only behaviour and photometry and not the paper's 37-motif labelling. Procedural learning was mixed: controls improved at reaching and silenced mice did not, but Arch mice never differed significantly, and maze speed did not reproduce. Evoked dopamine release in dCP and cCP held.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Mantas, Contestabile, Skara et al. (bioRxiv 2024) on dandiset 001828, which holds the paper's open field pose, kinematics and VAME motifs (some with fiber photometry), optogenetically evoked dLight release, water drop and forelimb reaching sessions with annotated events, and arrow maze pose. It tests evoked release in dCP against cCP, the photometry around the water drop and during open field movement, the locomotion of the PD models and Anxa1-silenced mice, the maze speed and reaching accuracy. The motif claims are blocked, as the dandiset's VAME labels are not the paper's; their analyses are shown on the dandiset's labels. The histology, RNA-seq, qPCR and nosepoke data of Figures 1 to 3 are not in the dandiset; the MitoPark RNA-seq counts are read from GEO GSE282753.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Mantas et al. (2024) from dandiset 001828

outcomes.notes: GEO GSE282753, public since 2026-10-20 and the paper's only RNA-seq deposit, holds one count table, MitoPark and control DANs at 10 weeks (5 MitoPark mice, as in the legend, and 7 controls, each with 3 to 12 technical libraries), and no cMfn2KO-early counts, so that half of the claim cannot be tested and the claim stays blocked. The answer (2026-10-21) found no other place for the cMfn2KO counts, and made the mouse the unit, with libraries summed per mouse, and the MitoPark half to be run and reported. Before the answer the MitoPark counts were not analysed (the earlier note counted 6 MitoPark mice; the table has 5). The MitoPark half holds under both readings, as the criterion judges them, where DESeq2 and edgeR agree. Summed per mouse, Anxa1 log2 fold change -1.02 at FDR 2.9e-05 (DESeq2) and -0.99 at FDR 7.5e-04 (edgeR exact test); with each library as a sample, -0.93 at FDR 5.0e-08 and 6.2e-08. Anxa1 counts per million are 90 to 222 in MitoPark mice and 258 to 446 in controls. GEO's supplementary files are this count table and an RPKM table of the same MitoPark libraries, and the series' design and its 92 samples describe MitoPark and control mice only (printed in the notebook).
deviations: DESeq2 is pydeseq2 0.5.4 and edgeR is edgepy (inmoose 0.9.1), a Python port, with TMM written out in the helper and the GLM common and tagwise dispersions (estimateGLMCommonDisp, estimateGLMTagwiseDisp) in place of estimateDisp, which the port lacks, so the edgeR reading is not edgeR's default route; R is not in the entry's environment.
All 7 control and 5 MitoPark mice are used; which the paper used is not given.

20 sessions, two Anxa1-Flp mice with the fiber in dCP and two in cCP, five powers each (0.1 to 2 mW). The answer (2026-10-21) named two readings, (a) all powers pooled per session and (b) each power alone, the session as unit in both, with baselines of 1 s and 2 s before train onset. Reading (a) was the one run before; (b) as a judged reading and the 2 s baseline for the session z-score are new. Under (a) the criterion holds with both z-scorings, both baselines and both windows; the dCP peak exceeds the baseline in 10 of 10 sessions and the cCP peak is lower, session z-score 1.21 against 0.61 (t = 3.94, p = 0.0010, Cohen's d 1.76), baseline z-score 2.30 against 1.19 (p = 0.0041) with 1 s and 1.93 against 1.03 (p = 0.0043) with 2 s. The 0 to 2 s window gives the same peaks. Under (b), 2 sessions against 2, it holds at 3 or 4 of 5 powers (p = 0.0039 to 0.037); it fails at 2 mW under every combination (p = 0.16 to 0.31) and at 0.1 mW except with the baseline z-score over 1 s (p = 0.056 and 0.11). dCP is above cCP in both mice at every power, and peaks rise with power (Spearman rho 0.81 dCP, 0.985 cCP). Per mouse, reported and not judged, the mean peak over powers is 1.23 and 1.20 in dCP and 0.56 and 0.66 in cCP. The first reading the criterion lists holds in full, so the outcome stays reproduced.
deviations: The dandiset holds dF/F, not the paper's z-scores; both z-score readings of the claims file are run.
The z-score against the baseline uses the same 1 s or 2 s window before each train as the baseline.

outcomes.notes: The claims file judges the claim under both its z-scorings; it holds under one and fails under the other. With the baseline z-score the dLight-cCP second-window change is positive and significant after Bonferroni over four tests in all four event and window combinations (p = 0.020 to 0.049) and over eight with 2 s windows (p = 0.040 and 0.047), and the DAT second (0.13 to 0.28) and cCP third (1.43 to 1.77) changes are positive. With the session z-score the cCP second-window change (0.29 to 0.36) is not significant under either correction (four tests p = 0.055 to 0.31). In every reading the cCP third window departs from the first far more than the second does (raw p = 0.0002 to 0.0004 against 0.005 to 0.077), the reverse of the legend (0.0028 for the second, 0.0148 for the third), and the DAT second-window change is far from significant (raw p = 0.13 to 0.89). Before the first verification the outcome was blocked (methods_underspecified), with the session z-score called the main reading; the verifier judged it partially reproduced, as the claims file ranks neither z-scoring, and it was changed.
deviations: The z-scoring of the photometry is not given; the claims file's two readings disagree here.

dLight-dCP correlates with speed above both shuffles (mean r = 0.067, 7 of 8 recordings positive, paired t-test p = 0.010 against permutation and 0.008 against circular shifts, Wilcoxon 0.023 and 0.016). Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP is positive in 9 of 10 recordings but not significantly (mean r = 0.066, p = 0.080 and 0.071, Wilcoxon 0.064); one recording (842430) is at r = -0.17. Without the seven recordings holding under 13 min of photometry, Anxa1 p = 0.097 and 0.089, and dLight-dCP p = 0.059 against permutation and 0.0499 against circular shifts. DAT GCaMP-dCP mean r = 0.032 (p = 0.22). Without mouse 687662, whose water drop file says Dat_cre, Anxa1 has mean r = 0.057, 7 of 8 positive, p = 0.21 and 0.18. Of the 19 open field files whose kinematics are not at lag 0 to the pose, five hold photometry (two Anxa1, two dLight-dCP, one dLight-cCP); with their speed moved by that lag, Anxa1 p = 0.082 and 0.073 and dLight-dCP p = 0.028 and 0.023 (dLight-dCP 6 of 8 positive, Wilcoxon p = 0.0547 against permutation). The Anxa1 speed-signal correlation peaks within 0.5 s of zero lag in 5 of 10 recordings and at -2.3 to 2.1 s in the others; the photometry and the speed are consistent with one clock where the files allow a check, not shown to share it in every recording. The criterion needs both groups above the shuffle at p < 0.05 under one reading, and Anxa1, the subject of the claim, misses it in every reading (p = 0.064 to 0.21). As for fig3e, a failed main part is a failure of the claim and not a partial result. This was partially reproduced before the first verification; the verifier judged it not reproduced in rounds 1 and 2, the change was proposed after round 2, and the third round agreed with it.
deviations: The legend counts 9 Anxa1 recordings of 9 mice and 8 dLight-dCP of 6; the dandiset holds 10 of 8 and 8 of 5, all used.

Under none of the four speed readings (tail base or mean of six points, raw or with positions below 0.9 confidence interpolated) is the day 4 difference significant (Sidak p = 0.11 to 0.41). A group effect with TeTx slower appears only with the tail base and cleaned positions (F = 4.98, p = 0.035; -21.8% on day 1, -17.7% on day 4); with raw tail base positions there is none (p = 0.75), and with the mean of six points TeTx mice are faster (raw, p = 0.021) or not different (p = 0.44). The immobility part is not tested. The tail base occupies the same pixel extent on every day (medians of the 1st and 99th percentiles 98 to 111 and 567 to 620 px in x, 185 to 232 and 699 to 706 px in y), so the pixel scale does not change between days. The speeds are unsmoothed apart from the interpolation, and the mean of six points is noisy (raw speeds 1.5 to 5.9 times those of the tail base in the group means); the outcome rests on these measures.
deviations: The dandiset holds pose only for the arrow maze; speed is computed from it in pixels per s, under the claims file's two point readings, and the smoothing, which is open, is run raw and with low-confidence positions interpolated.
17 control mice where the legend has 18.
Sidak's group comparisons are unpaired t-tests per day, Sidak-adjusted over the two days.
No immobility value exists in the dandiset or the paper, so immobility is not judged.

Rewards received are not in the dandiset (see fig6d-maze-preference-learning).

The answers (2026-10-21) fixed the readings. Day 1 and day 4 are the first and fourth training sessions (the files' test1 and test4, test4 falling 2 to 4 days after test1), the controls of both cohorts are one group, and the main run is the 17 mice recorded before the preprint (8 controls, 4 TeTx, 5 Arch; 8 + 4 + 5 fits the legend's F(2,14)), all mice being a variant. Before the answers the claim was blocked because the outcome turned on which mice were used. In the main run the control and TeTx parts hold and the Arch part fails. With every labelled reach, the preferred limb per mouse and 0.2 cm, interaction F(2, 13) = 4.42, p = 0.034; controls improve from 0.338 to 0.650 (Sidak p = 0.010); on day 4 controls exceed TeTx (0.239, p = 0.0014) but not Arch (0.428, p = 0.22); on day 1 TeTx do not differ (p = 0.994). One Arch mouse (842433) has no reach with its preferred limb on one day there. Without empty and unknown reaches, interaction p = 0.046, control improvement p = 0.020, TeTx below controls p = 0.016, Arch p = 0.34. With the preferred limb per session all 17 mice enter with the legend's df (2, 14), but the interaction misses (p = 0.060 and 0.085). Arch on day 4 fails in all eight readings of the main run (Sidak p = 0.044 to 0.34; the one below 0.05, at 0.1 cm, has an interaction p of 0.12), and at 0.1 cm the interaction misses in every reading (p = 0.069 to 0.27). Single exclusions make the criterion hold in 0 of 16 with the limb per mouse and 1 of 17 with the limb per session (Arch mouse 828027 left out, interaction p = 0.016, Arch day 4 p = 0.035). The variant with all mice holds at 0.2 cm under all four event and limb readings (interaction p = 0.0030 to 0.028). The Arch effect is present but weaker. On day 4 Arch accuracy is below the controls' in all eight readings of the main run (0.099 to 0.428 against 0.264 to 0.650), but never at Sidak p < 0.05 together with an interaction at p < 0.05, so the outcome is partial; the verifier judged it not reproduced, and the disagreement is recorded. The Arch day 1 sessions are labelled with the laser on after the first reach, a departure from the paper's protocol, and are used as day 1.
deviations: The Arch cohort's day 1 sessions are all labelled with the laser switched on after the first reach, where the Methods have it off on day 1; they are used as day 1.
Sessions of one mouse on one day (two mice) are pooled.
Sidak's tests after the RM two-way ANOVA are t-tests with Sidak adjustment (paired over the three groups for day 1 against day 4, unpaired over four comparisons between groups).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only behaviour and fiber photometry. The histology, RNA-scope and tracing images or counts, the qPCR of iPSC-derived neurons and the nosepoke counts of the self-stimulation and ratio tasks are not in it, so 16 claims of Figures 1 to 3 cannot be tested. GEO GSE282753 holds the MitoPark RNA-seq counts but not the cMfn2KO ones. No file holds a nosepoke, port, reward, zone, entry or trial object.
The arrow maze files hold DeepLabCut pose only. The Bonsai end-zone entries, reward deliveries and arena geometry behind Figure 6D are not in them.

86 open field sessions have session_id tmaze-..., 84 of them in files named ses-tmaze-..., although their descriptions, contents (VAME labels, kinematics, the open field DeepLabCut model) and frame counts are those of open field sessions.

Experimental groups, cohorts, days, test phases and light conditions are given only in free text inside session_description, with names that differ between experiments (ctrl, asc_acid, Ctrl 10-11 wks, Littermate control); the subject metadata carry no group.

Subject genotypes conflict across files. Mice with dLight (776769, 776770, 796284, 796287, 802369, 802372, 821709, 821710, 829248, 842388, 842395) are WT in their open field files and Anxa1-flp or Dat_cre in their other files, and 687662 is anxa1-flp in the open field and Dat_cre in reaching. Mouse 779575 is a control in the open field TeTx experiment and a TeTx mouse in the reaching cohort.

The paper's 37-motif VAME labelling is not in the dandiset. Its only labelling, VAME_42, has 42 labels (0 to 41) with no names or action categories, while the paper reports 37 motifs numbered up to 42 and grouped into categories; motif 42 is not a label and motif 28 is unused by the Figure 5 mice. Ten claims rest on the paper's motifs.

The VAME motif labels are stored with starting_time 0 on the frame grid of the pose and kinematics, but they explain linear speed best when placed 15 to 21 frames later (median 18, eta squared 0.69 against 0.49 as stored), about half the 30-frame VAME window, so a stored label is consistent with describing the window that starts at its frame. The files do not say how labels are placed in time, and motif onsets as stored come about 0.6 s early.

The 30 Hz z-scored open field photometry (FiberPhotometrySeriesZScored) is smoothed (its first and last 7 or 8 samples are held constant) and best matches the dF/F 0.1 s earlier; neither the smoothing nor the lag is documented.

The dandiset holds more photometry recordings and mice than the legends count (water drop, Anxa1 15 against 10, DAT 8 against 4, dLight-dCP 21 against 13, dLight-cCP 15 against 11; open field Anxa1 10 against 9) and fewer in some (open field DAT 6 against 7, arrow maze controls 17 against 18), without saying which recordings the paper used.

entries.name: 001828-mantas-2024
entries.title: Anxa1+ dopamine neurons, behaviour and photometry (Mantas, Contestabile, Skara et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Mantas, Contestabile, Skara et al. (bioRxiv 2024) on dandiset 001828, which holds the paper's open field pose, kinematics and VAME motifs (some with fiber photometry), optogenetically evoked dLight release, water drop and forelimb reaching sessions with annotated events, and arrow maze pose. It tests evoked release in dCP against cCP, the photometry around the water drop and during open field movement, the locomotion of the PD models and Anxa1-silenced mice, the maze speed and reaching accuracy. The motif claims are blocked, as the dandiset's VAME labels are not the paper's; their analyses are shown on the dandiset's labels. The histology, RNA-seq, qPCR and nosepoke data of Figures 1 to 3 are not in the dandiset; the MitoPark RNA-seq counts are read from GEO GSE282753.
